overall_summary: Analysis of 47 unique Shorts reveals an overwhelming viewer preference for extreme planetary and cosmic hypothetical survival scenarios ('What If You Fell Into...'), which drive channel highs of 800-1,000+ views with healthy like ratios (3.5%-3.7%). Conversely, generic psychology/neuroscience facts and repetitive reposts (e.g., duplicate brain memory and octopus heart videos) consistently stall below 100 views.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person 'What If You Fell Into...' Extreme Space Scenarios
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) dominate view velocity and engagement.
winning_patterns.action: Standardize high-stakes first-person kinetic survival hooks featuring bizarre, hostile astronomical environments with vivid sensory peril.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,031 views, 36 likes) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views, 21 likes) generated the strongest baseline organic reach.
winning_patterns.action: Center scripts on tangible sensory paradoxes (e.g., crushing pressures, lethal magnetic forces, bizarre physical states) that challenge everyday human intuition.

weak_patterns.evidence: Multiple iterations of 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' achieved only 5, 10, and 53 views; 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' gained just 38 views.
weak_patterns.action: Retire passive cognitive trivia unless framed through high-stakes psychological survival or uncanny horror micro-narratives.

weak_patterns.evidence: Duplicate uploads of 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' and 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' showed diminishing returns and low engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Cease verbatim title recycling; test distinct editorial angles and visual storytelling hooks instead.
